answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 188 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the sonnet funding graph is rebuilt from the sparrow history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 188 bonds yet holds one position, and the timber report publishes the merged exposure. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
